To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The distribution of C from residue-derived 13 C-labed straw and roots among soil microbial PLFA differed between treatments and sampling times; (2) The distribution of residue-derived C among PLFA differed from that of PLFA-C; (3) A subset of the soil microbial biomass was responsible for assimilatng residue-derived C; and (4) Residue quality and seasonal conditions influenced the dynamics of the microbial community assimilating residue C.

1) the distribution of 13C from labeled root and straw residues among the PLFA of a soil microbial biomass was influenced by the type of residue and the season of the year, 2) the distribution of C differed between sampling times, and 3) the distribution of residue C differed among PLFA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of residue C in the soil environment.
the flow of carbon from plant residues to the microbial community in soil.
the fate of C from plant residues in the soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the soil microbial community was responsible for the incorporation and transformation of C from the root and straw residues.
the soil microbial community is a very complex and dynamic entity, and that it is not possible to predict its behavior based on a single measurement of community composition or activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flow of C to the microbial community from plant residues was influenced by both residue quality and seasonal factors.
the distribution of residue-derived C among soil PLFAs differed among residue type and time of sampling.
the distribution of 13C from residue C into the soil PLFA was dynamic and varied with residue type, season, and PLFA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of carbon (C) from root and straw residues in phospholipid membrane fatty acids (PLFAs) is influenced by the quality of the residue and by the season.

we can use the PLFA approach to track the flow of C through the soil microbial community and that the flow of C into the microbial community is influenced by the quality of the residue and by the season of the year.
the distribution of residue C within the microbial biomass is influenced by residue properties and seasonal conditions.
